newsitem.title: UK: Fergie seals $1.6 million deal with Revlon -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Fergie seals $1.6 million deal with Revlon -- paper.

text.p: Britain's disgraced Duchess of York has signed a one million pound ($1.6 million) deal with U.S. cosmetics giant Revlon to market her own perfume, a British Sunday newspaper reported.

The former Sarah Ferguson, known widely as Fergie, could eventually make six million pounds ($10 million) from the deal and help wipe out her debts, which are said to be huge, according to the Sunday People.
It was not immediately possible to contact Revlon for comment.

The Sunday People said Fergie, whose reputation has been badly tarnished by a series of tawdry revelations about her sex life, would market her own "Duchess" perfume in the first major advertising campaign mounted by a figure in British royal circles.

A Revlon source was quoted by the paper as saying that the deal, expected to be officially announced in the next few weeks, would overshadow the one which top model Elizabeth Hurley had signed with rivals Estee Lauder.
"Fergie's ours. The Duchess of York will be our very own Liz Hurley," the source told the newspaper.
As well as appearing in advertisements across the globe, Fergie would present her own show on a televised shopping channel, the newspaper said.

"(Revlon boss) Ron (Perelman) has told Fergie that she needn't worry about her reputation in the States. She is still regarded as a member of the royal family and that makes her a very valuable property," the company source said.
If the story is confirmed it will come as a breath of fresh air for the beleaguered Ferguson, whose private life has been exposed in a series of books.
But it will undoubtedly pain Queen Elizabeth, since appearing in advertisements flouts royal convention. Last week Fergie was seen endorsing a new Olympus digital camera.

According to a book by former close friend Allan Starkie, Fergie first betrayed her husband, the queen's second son Prince Andrew, just three years after their marriage while she was pregnant with her second daughter.

A later affair with businessman John Bryan was revealed to the world in 1992 when a newspaper published photographs showing them half-naked and cavorting beside a swimming pool in the south of France.
The author said he acted as a go-between between Fergie and Bryan during their volatile four-year relationship and in the book portrayed a self-centred, egotistical and greedy couple.
In her own autobiography, Fergie described herself as a "national disgrace" and said she had never been suitable as a member of the royal family.
Fergie and Prince Andrew separated in 1992 and were divorced six months ago but are said to remain friends.
